does_not_refute: That SCHED_FIFO promotion would help. nice moves a thread within CFS; SCHED_FIFO is a different class that preempts CFS entirely, so the promotion experiment is still worth running by a bench that can. But the reasoning that motivated it - the reader is being starved of CPU - is now the weaker half.
leaves_open: What the load actually does. Cache or memory-bandwidth pressure, timer behaviour, and contention inside the test process are all untested. Nothing here identifies a mechanism; it removes one.
means: Load run at nice 19 breaks the assertion just as readily as load at nice 0 - 7 of 12 against 8 of 18, p = 0.70 - and both against 0 of 14 idle. Sixteen nice-19 threads get almost no CFS share against a nice-0 daemon, so if the mechanism were the daemon losing scheduler share to the load, nice 19 should have largely removed it. It does not.
refutes: The hypothesis this bench posted on #58 fifteen minutes earlier: that the contention route is the daemon's unpromoted reader losing CPU share. Losing SHARE is excluded. It was labelled as the cheap hypothesis when posted and it did not survive the first test aimed at it.
